clinical.rationale: Updated meta-analysis of RCTs on fluid choice in pediatric septic shock, a front-line ED resuscitation decision, supporting balanced crystalloids as default.

research.rationale: Standard PROSPERO-registered meta-analysis of RCTs updating a known question.

papers.one_line: Across 6 RCTs (10,308 children), balanced crystalloids did not reduce mortality but reduced renal replacement therapy, hyperchloraemia and hypernatraemia versus 0.9% saline.

summary.why_it_matters: 0.9% saline remains the most common bolus fluid for pediatric septic shock despite its high chloride content; fluid choice is a front-line ED resuscitation decision.
summary.design: PRISMA 2020, PROSPERO-registered systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of randomized trials of balanced crystalloids versus 0.9% saline in children (< 18 years) with sepsis or septic shock.
summary.key_findings: Six trials (10,308 children). Mortality 3.7% vs. 3.9% (RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.75-1.21); AKI not reduced (RR 0.76), renal replacement therapy reduced (RR 0.67, 0.48-0.92); hyperchloraemia (RR 0.65) and hypernatraemia (RR 0.59) reduced; hyperlactataemia more frequent (RR 1.17).
summary.bottom_line: Balanced crystalloids are an equally safe, physiologically preferable default, but offer no mortality benefit.

papers.one_line: In 99 pediatric CPR events with invasive airways, airway opening index >=0.35 was associated with improved survival to discharge and favorable neurological outcome.

summary.why_it_matters: Airway patency during CPR may affect ventilation and outcomes; the airway opening index (AOI) had only been described in adults.

summary.bottom_line: A capnography-derived airway patency metric is associated with pediatric CPR outcomes and merits validation as a quality target.

summary.bottom_line: Return after pediatric non-transport is rare; the risk factors identified can inform safer non-transport protocols.

clinical.rationale: First individual-level evidence linking hyperlocal gun violence to recurrent pediatric psychiatric emergencies; informs risk awareness rather than direct management.

research.rationale: Geocoded linkage of gun violence incidents to patient residences with survival analysis fills a clear evidence gap; single-center retrospective design.

papers.one_line: Gun violence within 400 meters of home in the prior 14 days more than doubled the hazard of recurrent psychiatric ED visit or admission in youth.

summary.why_it_matters: Pediatric mental health emergencies are rising, and little is known about whether hyperlocal community violence acutely triggers psychiatric crises at the individual level.
summary.design: Retrospective longitudinal cohort (preprint) of 4,730 youth <18 years with a psychiatric admission or ED visit at Cincinnati Children's, 2016-2024, using Cox models with geocoded gun violence exposure.
summary.key_findings: 34.3% had a recurrent psychiatric exacerbation; 41.5% were exposed to nearby gun violence. Exposure within 400 meters in the prior 14 days was associated with adjusted HR 2.45 (95% CI, 1.91-3.14), robust across alternative spatial and temporal definitions.
summary.bottom_line: Recent nearby gun violence may be an acute trigger of pediatric psychiatric crises and a target for post-incident outreach.

papers.methods_note: Single-center EHR cohort geocoded to police gun violence data + Cox survival analysis
